papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Subspace Construction via Symmetry-Preserving Cost Functions
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, results on convergence and gaps, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum subspace method for low-lying electronic energy states, tested on H4 chain and ring.

assertions.value: The authors state that, under certain conditions, their approach leads to a tridiagonal representation similar to that obtained with the Lanczos algorithm.
quotes: We show that, under certain conditions, our approach leads to a tridiagonal representation similar to that obtained with the Lanczos algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation I did not check line by line; the coordinator grades it.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a chemistry eigensolver, not an ML workload.

assertions.value: The authors test the algorithms as a proof of concept on H4 chain and ring, targeting both the ground-state energy and the charge gap.
quotes: As a proof of concept, we test the proposed algorithms on H4 chain and ring, targeting both the ground-state energy and the charge gap.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the test scope, p.1

assertions.value: The authors state that a significantly deep circuit would be required to fully match the performance of the Lanczos algorithm and that this is probably also associated with optimization issues.
assertions.anchor: Section on convergence of VQSM, near Fig. 9
quotes: Altogether, increasing the number of HEA layers NL improves the convergence rate, although a significantly deep circuit would be required to fully match the performance of the Lanczos algorithm and probably also associated with optimization issues.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in the convergence discussion

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Semi-Random Forests for Qubit-Efficient Recommender Systems
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methodology outline, results tables, conclusion, future work
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid recommender pipeline: dictionary learning, 5-qubit QAOA feature selection, and a 100-tree quantum semi-random forest, run in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 100-tree QsRF trained on the compressed codes matches full-feature baselines on ICM-150/500.
quotes: A 100-tree QsRF trained on these codes matches full-feature baselines on ICM-150/500.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says matches, while the conclusion says it outperforms a five-feature random forest; the two claims name different baselines.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QsRF yielded AUC = 0.8260, LogLoss = 0.2372, and nDCG@10 = 0.5942 in its end-to-end run.
quotes: QsRF yielded AUC = 0.8260, LogLoss = 0.2372, and nDCG@10 = 0.5942

assertions.value: The authors state that all QAOA circuits were executed on the PennyLane simulator with default noise-free backends and that validation on real quantum hardware is planned.
assertions.anchor: Section on cost analysis and Future Work
quotes: All QAOA circuits were executed on the PennyLane simulator [17] using default noise-free backends; we plan to validate our approach on real quantum hardware as it becomes available.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the simulator-only setup in the methods text

assertions.value: The authors state that on both the ICM-150 and ICM-500 splits, QsRL consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art quantum-based method.
quotes: On both the ICM-150 and ICM-500 splits of our content–metadata benchmark, QsRL consistently outperforms state of the art Quantum-based method.
assertions.reader_inference: The results table as extracted shows an ICM-150 nDCG@10 of 0.1483 for QsRL against 0.5929 for the random forest, which does not fit the conclusion; possible table typo, not checked against the figure.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum algorithm for finding minimum values in a Quantum Random Access Memory
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, algorithm, complexity analysis, K-means, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A Grover-based minimum search over data in a QRAM, with a K-means application.

assertions.value: The authors propose a quantum algorithm for finding the minimum value of a database that they describe as quadratically faster than its best classical analogs.
quotes: we present the proposal of a quantum algorithm for ﬁnding the minimum value of a database, which is quadratically faster than its best classical analogs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Complexity argument built on Durr-Hoyer; not machine-checked here.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup depends on the assumed QRAM, which is not built.

assertions.value: The authors assume a QRAM that stores the database values and perform an iterative search with an oracle that limits the searched values by controlling the states of the most significant qubits.
quotes: We assume a Quantum Random Access Memory (QRAM) that stores values from a database and perform an iterative search based on an oracle whose role is to limit the searched values by controlling the states of the most signiﬁcant qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the QRAM assumption, p.1

assertions.value: The authors assume that, in the quantum version of K-means, the distances between each point and all centroids are stored in QRAM in constant time, that is, O(1).
quotes: We assume that in the quantum version of K-means, the distances between each observed point
are stored in QRAM in constant time, that is, O(1).
assertions.reader_inference: Constant-time QRAM loading carries the claimed K-means benefit.

papers.title_in_file: Piecewise Polynomial Tensor Network Quantum Feature Encoding
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, conclusions; sections 2-5 and the examples skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A tensor-network method to embed continuous variables into quantum circuits as piecewise polynomial features.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate the potential of PPTNQFE through efficient point evaluations of solutions of discretized differential equations and in modeling functions with localized features such as jump discontinuities.
quotes: We demonstrate the potential of PPTNQFE through efficient point evaluations of solutions of discretized differential equations and in modeling functions with localized features such as jump discontinuities.

assertions.value: The authors state that these embeddings are not inherently superior or inferior to others and do not confer any QA.
quotes: It is crucial to note that these embeddings are not inherently superior or inferior to others and do not confer any QA.

assertions.value: The authors state that converting TN gates to hardware-native gates may introduce significant overhead and that the effects of statistical and hardware-induced noise on these embeddings were not explored.
quotes: However, converting TN gates to those native to quantum hardware may introduce significant overhead.
Additionally, the effects of statistical and hardware-induced noise on these embeddings were not explored in this work.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Kernels for Audio Deepfake Detection Using Spectrogram Patch Features
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methodology, results, limitations, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A shallow quantum kernel (Q-Patch) for audio spoofing detection, evaluated in ideal simulation on a 100-sample set.

assertions.value: The authors report that Q-Patch achieved an AUROC of 0.87 and an EER of 14.8%, outperforming the RBF-SVM on the same patch-level descriptors and a compact CNN.
quotes: Q-Patch achieves an AUROC of 0.87 and an EER of 14.8%, outperforming both the radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) trained on the same patch-level descriptors and the compact convolutional neural network (Tiny CNN) trained directly on spectrograms.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract gives the RBF-SVM AUROC as 0.82; with 20 dev samples the gap is within noise.

assertions.value: The authors build a balanced 100-sample subset of LJ Speech with 50 bona fide and 50 spoofed utterances, make the spoofs with additive Gaussian noise and spectral distortions, and split it into 80 training and 20 development samples.
quotes: we construct a balanced 100-sample subset from LJ Speech [8], consisting of 50 bona fide utterances and 50 spoofed utterances.
The spoofed samples are generated from the original recordings using additive Gaussian noise and spectral distortions as a controlled proxy for authenticity manipulation.
We then partition this 100-sample set into 80 training and 20 development (dev) samples with preserved class balance and no overlap between splits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III states the dataset construction
assertions.reader_inference: The spoofs are synthetic noise, not modern TTS or voice conversion attacks.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the dev split contains only 20 samples, the AUROC and EER are point estimates from a feasibility study, and that no physical quantum-hardware runs were performed; kernel fidelities were computed under ideal simulation.
quotes: Because the dev split contains only 20 samples, the reported AUROC and EER should be interpreted as point estimates from a compact feasibility study rather than as statistically definitive performance claims.
No physical quantum-hardware runs were performed in this study; kernel fidelities were computed under ideal simulation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV and the implementation text state the limits

papers.title_in_file: Efficient Mutation Testing of Quantum Machine Learning Models
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, mutation operations, experimental setup, results, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: New mutation operations and a directed mutant generation method for testing quantum neural networks.

assertions.value: The authors report that their mutation operations generate up to 6,784 mutants for BC with ZFM and SU2, a reduction of 9.5 times from 64,576 under the same configuration with prior mutation operations.
assertions.anchor: Section V-E, Reduction of Redundant Mutants
quotes: these mutation operations can generate up to 6,784 mutants (BC with ZFM and SU2), a reduction of 9.5 times, down from 64,576 under the same model configuration with prior mutation operations.

assertions.value: The authors report that APGC was the most effective operation in killing data samples for all datasets and model configurations, with an average mutation score of 90.68% for the QNN models and 100.00% for the QCNN models.
quotes: APGC was the most effective operation in killing data samples for all datasets and model configurations, with an average mutation score of 90.68% for the QNN models and 100.00% for the QCNN models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the mutants were executed on the classical simulators provided by Qiskit-Aer v0.17.2.
quotes: For execution, we test on the classical simulators provided by Qiskit-Aer v0.17.2.
assertions.reader_inference: No hardware run or noise model is reported; I found no limitations section.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum State Preparation via Neural Network Encoding in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, framework, results, runtime, limitations, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A classical neural network predicts the parameters of a fixed circuit that prepares FRQI image states, tested on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report fidelities up to 0.992 on unseen images from MNIST and Fashion-MNIST and a reduction of more than 5000-fold in per-data-instance runtime.
quotes: We validate our method on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, achieving fidelities up to 0.992 on unseen images and reducing the per-data-instance runtime by more than 5000-fold.

assertions.value: The authors report that the per-image optimization baseline, averaged over 10 samples, requires 3.27 s per image and was stopped once a fidelity of F ≥ 0.950 was reached.
quotes: Averaged over 10 samples, the baseline requires 3.27 s per image
terminating early once a fidelity of F ≥ 0.950 is reached.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup rests on a 10-sample baseline with a different circuit architecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that all experiments used low-resolution (32 × 32) grayscale benchmarks, that scaling to higher resolutions would require deeper circuits or hierarchical encodings whose trainability remains open, and that hardware noise and finite shot effects have not been evaluated.
quotes: All experiments used low-resolution (32 × 32) grayscale benchmarks; scaling to higher resolutions would require deeper circuits or hierarchical encodings whose trainability remains open.
All simulations used ideal state-vector backends; hardware noise and finite shot effects have not been evaluated.

papers.title_in_file: Analysis of Atom-level pretraining with QM data for Graph Neural Networks Molecular property models
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methods, experiments, results, conclusions; supplementary material not in the file
papers.what_it_is: A classical graph-network study: pretraining a Graphormer on quantum-mechanics atomic properties improves TDC benchmark results.

assertions.value: The authors report that atom-level pretraining notably enhances model performance compared to training from scratch for 21 of the 22 datasets.
quotes: These results show that atom-level pretraining notably enhances model performance compared to training from scratch for 21 of the 22 datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: QM means quantum-mechanics data used to pretrain a classical network; no quantum computer is involved.

assertions.value: The authors report visually observing that the atom-level pretrained method gives a more Gaussian-like distribution of the features.
quotes: Visually, we can observe that the atom-level pretrained method results in a more Gaussian-like distribution of the features.

assertions.value: The authors state that pretraining used a public dataset of 136k organic molecules and that results are reported for 5 different seeds.
quotes: For pretraining, we used a publicly available dataset [13] consisting of 136k organic molecules.
atom-level QM pretrained with all properties for 5 different seeds
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 3 and Section 4 state the setup
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states no explicit limitations section.
